feasibility: Use exactly eligible=true rows in the saved feasibility report. Every excluded row and its words stays in the coverage ledger, never counted as generated.
fixed: outermost word-box edges per eligible row

generators.equal_gaps: Set all n-1 gaps to their exact rational average; no score is consulted.
generators.empirical_gap_permutation: Independently uniformly permute the observed n-1 nonnegative gaps per eligible row; keep their multiset and sum. Duplicate gap values give repeated permutations with equal multiset probability.

evaluation.population: Eligible rows only, partners restricted to that same population. Report actual excluded-row name counts separately; never impute a full-page comparison.
evaluation.statistic: Count each endpoint once with an identical-word (or declared family) partner on another row of its page, horizontal center distance <=15px. Original support centers; equal-gap centers exact rational, random centers exact half-pixel.
evaluation.outputs: Observed/equal-gap endpoints and pairs; all per-page and pooled random scores; first random trial centers per page, selected before scoring; finite-MC summaries; exact possible center ranges; gap-arrangement counts and exclusions. Report both successful and unsuccessful comparisons.
evaluation.selection: No target-score optimization, parameter search, favorable page removal, or additional tolerance search.

interpretation: Gap exchangeability is a declared toy assumption, not independently established historical evidence. Gaps may contain verse/stop markers or diacritics; this interval renderer does not reconstruct their ink, kashida, glyph joins or vertical placement. Frozen widths and line breaks may already encode design. Success establishes interval feasibility only; failure excludes only these spacing rules, not human production. Neither outcome supplies origin likelihoods.
stop_rule: Complete this six-page feasibility and spacing report, verify it, and decide whether a more realistic independently validated comparator merits held-out evaluation. No automatic corpus expansion.
